notes.title: Isle of Reveries looks like a fun classic Zelda-like with some interesting game mechanics
notes.notes:
Inspired clearly by the likes of classic Zelda and the Game Boy Color, Isle of Reveries is one for fans of retro games that want something new and fresh.

Read the full article here: https://www.gamingonlinux.com/2025/03/isle-of-reveries-looks-like-a-fun-classic-zelda-like-with-some-interesting-game-mechanics/

[b]Nintendo Switch Pro controllers are now compatible![/b] I played through the demo both on a Windows PC and SteamDeck using an official Switch Pro Controller to confirm.

[b]Pushing blocks has been revamped![/b] You can now push a moveable block by walking into it like in GameBoy Zelda games -- no need to press the A button anymore.

notes.title: Demo Tweaks and Previews | December Progress Update
notes.notes:
Hello!

Thank you all for playing the Isle of Reveries demo and leaving feedback and reviews! A lot of progress was made on updating the demo and the full game:

[h3]🦉 Kickstarter Coming Soon![/h3]
A Kickstarter campaign for Isle of Reveries is set to launch in February 2025! Your support will let us fully realize the vision for Isle of Reveries, and include cool extras like mini-games, a Zelda 2 style dungeon, and more.

Follow Isle of Reveries on Kickstarter by [url=https://www.kickstarter.com/projects/desertcucco/isle-of-reveries/]clicking here[/url].

[h3]🎮 Demo Updates & Tweaks[/h3]
A number of updates to the demo version were pushed in December, including:
[list]
[*]Map screen now shows if a room has a staircase in it.
[*]Water and pits are now more forgiving, letting you escape falling in during a brief 0.5s window.
[*]Enemies have a 0.5s buffer before they start moving and attacking when the player enters the sam grid as them.
[/list]

notes.title: UPDATED: Nintendo Switch Pro Controllers Work!
notes.notes:
[b]Nintendo Switch Pro controllers now work![/b] I made some updates and played through the demo both on a Windows PC and SteamDeck using an official Switch Pro Controller to confirm.

///////

[b]ORIGINAL POST:[/b]
[i]First off, I want to thank everyone that's played the Isle of Reveries Demo and either left a review or posted their feedback in the Community Hub!

It's come to my attention that there are some bugs when using a Nintendo Switch controller (Pro Controller, USB GameCube controller, etc). I believe this comes from the engine I'm using to build Isle of Reveries in.

I'll be trying to resolve these issues, but I [b]highly recommend playing with an Xbox controller[/b] (of any kind) or using the keyboard. I apologize for the inconvenience.[/i]

notes.title: Play the Isle of Reveries Demo on Steam Deck!
notes.notes:
Although Valve doesn't provide verification for game demos at this time, Isle of Reveries is being developed and tested with Steam Deck in mind, so the demo is fully compatible by default. No need to fiddle with Proton versions or gamepad configurations!

The [url=https://store.steampowered.com/app/3154880/Isle_of_Reveries_Demo]Isle of Reveries Demo[/url] has received a couple of reviews from players that primarily played on Steam Deck:

----

[i]"I'm a big fan of both traditional 2-D top-down Zelda and the GBC pixel art aesthetic, so IoR is right up my street. Clearly a lot of love and attention has gone into crafting this demo. Looking forward to the full game."[/i] -- Steam reviewer

[i]"i am a bird"[/i] -- Steam reviewer

----

notes.title: Demo Patch - 11.19.24
notes.notes:
Added a little patch fixing the following:

[list]
[*]Added an 0.5s buffer period when entering a grid before enemies can move around/attack.
[*]A couple of bugs with the boss that can occur between phases if specific actions are triggered.
[*]Minor layout adjustment in the dungeon.
[*]Decreased volume for the opening jingle.
[/list]

I would like to improve the keyboard layout as well. If you have suggestions for a better keyboard layout, please post in the discussion board.
